sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: For some bosses, it's less about having the perfect CV and more about the way you think, the questions you ask and whether you're prepared to take a chance.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Six business founders and leaders share the qualities they notice most and the advice they would give to people trying to get ahead.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlotte Tilbury says one of the biggest things that has driven her career is refusing to let other people set limits on what she can do.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Nothing is impossible in life - it's only your own limitations you give yourself." The beauty mogul says there will always be naysayers, and there were plenty of people who told her she was "mad" or that her ideas would not work but it's important to ignore them.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Tilbury recommends trying not to think of setbacks as mistakes, but as opportunities to rethink and improve.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "I don't think about mistakes, I think mistakes are opportunities," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Many of the biggest challenges she faced ultimately made her a stronger business leader and "challenge is opportunity and it leads you to greater places".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Bowes-Lyon, co-founder of deodorant brand Wild, says attitude matters far more than having the perfect set of skills.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "For me, it's 90% attitude and 10% skills, as skills can be taught, attitude can't." One thing he wishes he had realised earlier is that even successful people do not always feel as confident as they appear and "everyone is faking it until they're making it".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: If you find yourself at a job interview, Bowes-Lyon says it's really important to have a few questions at the end as "candidates who say they have no questions rarely get the job".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: One question he recommends asking the interviewer is what success in the job looks like.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Read more about how Charlie Bowes-Lyon runs Wild Marcia Kilgore, the serial entrepreneur behind brands including Beauty Pie and Soap and Glory, says curiosity is one of the main qualities she looks for when hiring.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She values people who will "roll their sleeves up, ask lots of questions and think about how they can be useful".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Kilgore also says good communication is crucial as she realised early on in her career that a lack of communication is often the reason things break down.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Her advice to communicate well in the workplace is to "listen to what's being asked and take a breath or five" before responding.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Your response doesn't have to be immediate, but it does have to be considered." Read more about how Marcia Kilgore built her beauty brands.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Anabel Kindersley, CEO and co-owner of Neal's Yard Remedies, says one of the best ways to build your skills is to keep saying yes to new opportunities.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Do everything and say yes to everything - it might feel uncomfortable but do it anyway," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: It is an approach that has shaped her own varied career, from working as a child actress to becoming an author and later moving into business.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She adds that honesty really matters and you should be truthful about your experience and confident in what you can offer.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: When hiring, Kindersley says she looks for people with "equal EQ as IQ", valuing emotional intelligence alongside ability.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Nunn, group chief executive of Lloyds Banking Group, says curiosity, resilience and an increasing willingness to think about how AI tools can also be used in the future are some of the skills he values most in his employees.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He also really puts an emphasis on hiring people who are good at working in a team as "at the heart of most jobs is the ability to work together in support of something much bigger".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: His advice for building experience is to take on opportunities that are outside your comfort zone.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Nunn says he was "terrified" about taking on retail roles earlier in his career, but found they gave him valuable experience.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "If something feels risky, try and do it as you'll learn more from it and it'll build breadth around your CV that you didn't have previously." Read about Charlie Nunn's top ways to manage your money.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: James Reed, chairman and chief executive of recruitment company Reed, says one of the biggest mistakes people make is thinking about what an employer can do for you rather than what you can offer in return.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "The biggest mistake is thinking that the world owes you a living," he says and instead suggests you should ask yourself: "How am I the solution to an employer?" As AI is increasingly used in recruitment, Reed says applicants need to think about how their skills are being picked up by technology as well as by a person.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Try and mirror the job description with your skills and experiences in your application," he says, so that the match between what an employer is looking for and what you can offer is clear.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He describes AI as "a wonderful tool", but says it should not replace your own judgement or voice – the aim is for it to strengthen an application rather than expect it to do the work for you.

sentences.text: Fire and smoke rise at EMCO's ammunition storage facility near Gorni Varpishta in central Bulgaria Bulgaria is investigating the cause of an overnight fire at an ammunition storage site run by a private defence company.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev said the authorities "are not ruling out outside interference" in the incident in central Bulgaria.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: No-one was injured in the blaze that triggered a series of explosions.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: EMCO company, whose weapons are used by Ukraine against invading Russian forces, said the fire at its site was sabotage and that human error was "completely ruled out".
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: It did not say who might be responsible.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: The latest incident follows last month's fire and blasts at another EMCO ammunition warehouse in the area.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: In a statement, EMCO said the storage facility that was burned this time - near the central village of Gorni Varpishta, some 170km (106 miles) east of the capital Sofia -   had not been used for months and was inspected just 20 days ago, when full compliance with all regulations was confirmed.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: It cited a number of similar incidents at Bulgarian defence firms since 2011, saying that the latest was "no exception to the series of acts of sabotage against the Bulgarian defence industry".
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: "As the EU and Nato member state most severely affected by such actions, Bulgaria must join the collective effort to prevent and neutralise these attacks," EMCO said.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: The firm is run by Bulgarian arms dealer Emilian Gebrev, who Bulgarian prosecutors allege has already been targeted by Russian agents.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: This includes a poisoning attempt in 2015 of Gebrev, his son and another company employee - three Russian nationals were later charged in absentia for attempted murder.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: Bulgaria is a major weapons supplier to Ukraine, as it continues to repel a full-scale Russian invasion launched in 2022.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: And although Sofia has recently halted state-owned arms supplies to Ukraine, Bulgarian private defence companies continue such transfers.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: Russia appears to have recently escalated its sabotage campaign across Europe.
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: Last week, Germany said Russia was responsible for August's drone attack at Leipzig's airport - a claim denied by Moscow as "absurd".
sentences.article_title: Bulgaria investigates fire at weapons  site that owner calls sabotage

sentences.text: There have also been a number of suspicious fires at defence facilities from Italy to Estonia, with some of the affected countries blaming Russia.

sentences.text: One of Hugo's owners, Lisa Masters, said he was "a big softie, like an oversized dog" A Shire horse that has entered the record books as the world's tallest living horse could exceed his height as he is still growing, his owner has said.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: Hugo, who lives in Towcester, Northamptonshire, has already reached an "abnormal" 199cm tall, about 6.5ft, or 19.2 hands, to the withers or ridge at the base of the neck.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: Guinness World Records said the four-year-old's stature was officially assessed by a vet and he was measured without shoes to ensure an accurate result.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: Owner Brett Masters said Hugo received "a huge amount of care" from a chiropractor, dentist, vet and masseuse, meaning he lived a "five-star lifestyle".
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: Shire horses are known for their height and their large stature means they are able to pull heavy weight, which is why they have been historically used as working horses on farms and for transport.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: The tallest and heaviest horse ever documented , external was a Shire gelding named Sampson, who was later renamed Mammoth - bred by Thomas Cleaver of Toddington Mills in Bedfordshire, which stood at 2.19 metres - or 7ft 2.5 in - in 1850.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: Hugo has his teeth checked twice a year by his dentist, Hannah Masters, from Tove Valley Shire Horses, said the breed was his passion.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: He was approached by officials from Guinness World Records as Hugo was "locally famous", and they had been told: "There is this really big horse, you need to speak to these guys." Masters said that when he acquired Hugo - at the age of 18 months - he had no idea he was "very tall, abnormally tall".
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: "He's still got three years of growing left, he won't stop until he's about eight and a half, he's only a baby," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: "It will cause issues, so we have to be very careful with him.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: "He has a chiropractor, has regular massages, the dentist visits every six months, and the vet checks him all the time as his growing plates are hyperactive.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: "He has lots of supplements and a careful feed regime.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: "He lives a five-star lifestyle, he wants for nothing." Brett Masters said when Hugo goes out and about, people stop to admire him Masters added: "Every time he goes out, people stop, they film him, shout at you that 'he's massive'.
sentences.article_title: 'He's massive!' Meet Hugo, the world's tallest horse

sentences.text: "He's very happy, and he just loves a good fuss," Masters added.

sentences.article_title: 'Batman mansion' owner hits back in bats row

sentences.text: Mentmore Towers, in rural Buckinghamshire, was served a listed-building repairs notice in August, urging the owners to carry out a survey of the flying mammals and repair masonry.

sentences.text: However, a spokesman for the country house, owned by property tycoon Simon Halabi, said its "own Batman team has already been on the case" with surveys and ecological investigations.
sentences.article_title: 'Batman mansion' owner hits back in bats row

sentences.article_title: 'Batman mansion' owner hits back in bats row

sentences.text: "We are also aware of works on-site that have been carried out without planning permission which we've looked into and are taking appropriate enforcement action on," the Conservative councillor added.
sentences.article_title: 'Batman mansion' owner hits back in bats row

sentences.text: Campaign group Save Britain's Heritage said the local authority ordered Halabi to carry out urgent repairs to its deteriorating roof in the notice.
sentences.article_title: 'Batman mansion' owner hits back in bats row

sentences.article_title: 'Batman mansion' owner hits back in bats row

sentences.text: Red Bay RNLI spent seven hours at sea Six people have been rescued after a 46ft yacht got into difficulty off the coast of Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: Red Bay Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) spent seven hours at sea in the early hours of Saturday morning off Cushendall, County Antrim.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: Belfast Coastguard received a distress call from the boat, which had been travelling from Oban in Scotland to Portugal.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: The yacht lost all power and steering after making contact with a fish farm in Red Bay, in 60 knots of wind, causing it to become trapped.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: A lifeboat was launched at 03:22 BST, with an inshore lifeboat also launched.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: In a statement Red Bay RNLI described the weather conditions as "difficult" due to "Force 9 gusting winds, driving rain and the darkness of night".
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: The RNLI crew observed that those on the yacht were safe and, given the difficult weather and sea conditions, the decision was made "for the sailors to remain onboard the yacht and for the lifeboat to standby until daylight broke" at 07:30.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: At 09.30 the lifeboat crew "successfully freed the yacht from the fish farm and brought the sailors safely to Glenarm".
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: Those on the yacht stayed onboard the vessel while it was towed by the RNLI, who said there were no injuries.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: The yacht is now receiving repairs.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: Speaking following the call out, Paddy McLaughlin, Red Bay RNLI Coxswain said: "This was a challenging call out in difficult weather conditions, but we were delighted to bring the sailors to safety, and we would like to wish them well.
sentences.article_title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm

sentences.text: "We would also like to commend our colleagues in the Coastguard and thank our crew who responded quickly in the middle of the night, launched our lifeboats in darkness and made their way to the scene in what were gale force conditions, and for then spending seven hours at sea."

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: MPs share personal stories in assisted dying debate MPs have voted against proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.

sentences.text: The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill would have allowed adults with fewer than six months to live to apply to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: A similar bill in the last parliamentary session was supported by MPs before stalling in the House of Lords .
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: The decision from MPs on Friday rules out the prospect of changes to the law on assisted dying in the short term.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: The bill tabled by Labour MP Lauren Edwards will make no further progress, although MPs and peers could make another attempt in the next parliamentary session.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Assisted dying is an issue that has been debated for hundreds of hours in Parliament over the last two years and would have represented one of the biggest societal changes in recent years had it been approved.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: MPs were given a free vote, meaning they were not required to vote along party lines.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Safeguards within the bill included a requirement that a person applying for an assisted death had the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: But critics said it included too few measures to protect vulnerable people from being coerced into ending their lives, while some say improving palliative care should be the priority.

sentences.text: Apple has launched its most expensive iPhone ever - a foldable handheld that costs at least £1,999 and marks the first major iPhone design change in almost 20 years.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: The iPhone Duo is a gamble by new boss John Ternus, who took over from long-time chief executive Tim Cook this month.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: Apple is entering the foldable phone market comparatively late, following the likes of South Korea's Samsung and China's Huawei.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: Ternus told an audience at Apple's California headquarters: "Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together".
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: Apple's model, he claimed "redefine[s] the experience of using a foldable phone".
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: In the US, prices start at $1,999, but can go up to $3,200.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: It has taken eight years to develop, something Ternus was directly involved in after spending many years as a top executive inside Apple's hardware division.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: When unfolded, it looks like a small iPad and a wider iPhone when it is folded.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: Ternus said: "It's entirely new and at the same time remarkably familiar.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: A similar size to your passport, it feels familiar to hold and comfortable to use with one hand." But the product is facing established competitors.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: "The real fight is China, where Huawei owns nearly 80% of foldables," said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president for data and analytics, devices at IDC EMEA.
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: Apple unveiled its new iPhone Duo as part of a launch event in Cupertino, California on Wednesday Ben Wood, chief analyst at technology research firm FDM CCS Insight, said it was likely Ternus's promotion was timed specifically "to coincide with what will be arguably one of the biggest iPhone launches for many years".

sentences.text: Altering the design of the iPhone may address some criticism that Apple has yet to land a major product hit or truly exciting innovation since the first iPhone came out in 2007.

sentences.text: Previously, the highest starting price of the newest iPhone was $900 (£664).
sentences.article_title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone

sentences.text: Or, he said, it could be the company's next Apple Watch which, while not as popular as the iPhone, is bought by millions of people each year.

Wood noted that the current market for foldable smartphones from the likes of Samsung and Huawei make up only 2% of smartphone sales.

sentences.text: York, pictured, is one of the cities where the regional mayor plans to limit the new levy to 5% of an overnight stay Labour's regional mayors in England have pledged to cap a new fee on visitors' overnight stays at 5%, after hospitality bosses warned it could put jobs at risk.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Local leaders are set to gain new powers to charge an uncapped levy, dubbed a "tourist tax", as a percentage of the cost of hotels, bed and breakfasts and other types of accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: But the Labour mayors in 10 city regions said they would voluntarily limit the charge if they do apply it, adding that they had listened to concerns over costs.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Reform UK's two regional mayors and the two Conservative ones are likely to oppose any levy given criticism from their national parties of the policy.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In a letter to Chancellor John Healey and Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner, the Labour metro mayors said 5% represented a "reasonable ceiling" on the tax.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "It provides a balance of ensuring that local levies are not excessive, or vary significantly between regions, while also leaving room for local variation as appropriate," they added.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: They added this would still allow for "meaningful investment" in local areas, whilst stressing any future levies in their areas would be "subject to local consultation".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The letter was signed by Labour mayors in London, Greater Manchester, Liverpool City Region, West Midlands, North East, West of England, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, East Midlands and York and North Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The government had earlier pledged to protect budget holidays "by making sure low-cost accommodation always pays lowest levy" and said the extra cash could be invested in high streets and local transport.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: While Labour mayors have backed the new levy, others have expressed caution or signalled they will not bring it in.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Local leaders, including heads of Foundation Strategic Authorities where there is no mayor, will need to clarify by early 2028 how the revenue raised should be reinvested.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: They will also be allowed to offer exemptions, such as for campsites.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: However, mayors will not be allowed to exempt whole localities within their regions from the tax, to avoid creating confusion for visitors and businesses.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The government said it would introduce a bill to Parliament "in due course" to bring in the levy, which would apply to both Britons and people visiting from abroad.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Leading trade body UKHospitality has hit back, saying the levy means "jobs are now at risk".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Its chief executive Allen Simpson claimed it would add about £100 to £120 on average to the cost of a family holiday in England, amid fears mayors would make use of the fact there is, in theory, no upper limit for the levy.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "We know, don't we, that local government is struggling for funds - it was hit very hard by austerity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: A 5% tourist tax for overnight stays was introduced in Edinburgh in July The idea was first raised under former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in November and is similar to schemes running in Scotland and European destinations.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Two cities in England already run their own voluntary schemes - a £1 per room, per night City Visitor Charge in Manchester, introduced when Burnham was mayor of the region, and a £2 nightly charge in Liverpool.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: These are business-led schemes where hotels choose to pool the money raised to support local tourism.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Until now, regional mayors have not had the power to bring such fees in themselves - but they argue it is needed to boost economic growth.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Conservative Mayor of Tees Valley Ben Houchen ruled out , external introducing any tourist tax last year.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: John Chappell, who runs five caravan parks in Skegness, Lincolnshire, told BBC Your Voice that many English tourist resorts have visitors on tight budgets already struggling with the cost of car travel.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: He said an extra cost would "kill the industry off".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "Tourists are the saviours of our resorts, not the demons and ill thought-out ideas like these show how out of touch with reality politicians are," he added.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The taxes are common in Europe and the rest of the world, with New York, Amsterdam and Rome applying overnight charges to accommodation stays to fund local services.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: However, they are capped in several European cities.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In Scotland local authorities can charge a visitor levy on overnight accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In Edinburgh, the rate is 5% for those staying overnight in hotels, bed and breakfasts and self-catering facilities - capped at five nights.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: It has had a mixed reaction , with some praising extra investment but Scottish Ballet responded by cutting performances while criticising the "unsustainable economics of touring in Edinburgh".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In Wales, a capped levy of £1.30 per person per night is set to be introduced in April next year, but it will be up to local authorities to decide whether to roll it out.

sentences.text: The new battery-electric TransPennine Express trains are set to enter service in 2034 Work to create the UK's first battery-electric trains for long-distance main line services is set to begin in 2028, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The 29 new Adessia Stream trains are expected to enter service in 2034 and will be built at Alstom's Litchurch Lane factory in Derby.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The government said the investment of almost £1bn would help support more than 350 jobs at Alstom and a further 6,000 jobs across the UK supply chain.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the new trains would deliver "faster, more reliable journeys to the north and thousands of British jobs for the next generation".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The managing director UK at Alstom said the fleet would transform journeys across northern England He added: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Today, that starts to change." The DfT said the trains would help deliver the TransPennine Route Upgrade's aim to boost capacity by 30%, with thousands of additional seats a day across the Pennines by the early to mid-2030s.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: They will run between key destinations across the north including Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: On sections of the railway that are not electrified, where trains currently use diesel engines, the new electric models would be able to run without emissions, the government said.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The DfT added journey times would be cut by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds, and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The trains will be bought by rolling stock company Rock Rail and leased to TransPennine Express, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Alstom, which boasts the largest rolling stock train manufacturing site outside of China, secured a £370m contract in 2024 to produce 10 new London Elizabeth line trains.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: This came less than three months after a redundancy consultation put 1,300 jobs at risk at its Litchurch Lane factory, which dates back to 1876.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Rob Whyte, managing director UK at Alstom, called the latest agreement a "landmark moment for Britain's railway".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: He said: "We're absolutely delighted.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It's fantastic news for Alstom as a company but also for the city of Derby and the East Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "It's a great opportunity for us to continue our legacy.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "Unite's Alstom members have worked tirelessly in campaigning to ensure Derby's proud history of train making continues well into the future," she added.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander spoke to the BBC at Alstom, next to one of the new Elizabeth line trains.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: She said: "It's fantastic news that a city like Derby, that's got such a proud railway heritage, is also going to be manufacturing that new fleet of trains for the north of England as well.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It's about building the railway that the country needs to support the economy, but it's also about making sure that, in our economic heartlands - places like Derby - we've got really high skilled jobs for the future.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "This contract alone means 40 extra apprentices here.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It secures 350 jobs at this facility and will support over 5,000 jobs in the wider supply chain as well." In a statement, DfT said journeys on the new fleet would be "quieter, smoother and more reliable", while offering "improved accessibility, more luggage space and onboard wi-fi".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Step-free boarding - the "elimination of gaps between the train and platform" - are also being promised as part of a commitment to accessibility, alongside three dedicated wheelchair spaces, two accessible toilets, family-friendly areas and cycle and buggy storage on each train.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Anthropic makes the AI tool Claude, which is used as a chatbot and as a tool to help coding A top safety researcher at Anthropic has warned AI is advancing so quickly he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Evan Hubinger said in a post on X , external the risk from the models which currently exist was "low" but he was "worried" the technology might develop and improve itself soon to the point where it posed an existential risk to humanity.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: He did not spell out how he thought AI systems could in future result in humans being wiped out.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: But his comments are the latest in a series of increasingly stark warnings about AI, with the debate shifting from whether it truly poses a risk to how big that risk is.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Hubinger's intervention was in response to another post on X , external from Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who has just quit Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: "Neither company is acting responsibly," he wrote.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: "These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionise any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources." OpenAI has been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Dame Wendy Hall, a computer scientist who advises the UN on AI, told the BBC she was "shocked" by Hubinger and Coxon's social media posts.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: She told the World at One on BBC Radio Four some of it could be "PR and marketing" however, as Anthropic and OpenAI raced towards highly anticipated stock market debuts.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: But she added: "Why would someone want to say that?
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: He told the BBC governments had to come together to "collaborate" about what a treaty based on the development of superintelligence should look like.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: "Unless governments take these warnings seriously enough and step up to it, the pace of development could mean that we end up with problems before we've started to look at whether it is an issue for us or not," he said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Separately, the Financial Times reported , external Anthropic withheld its latest model from the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI), one of the leading bodies in the world for assessing AI risk.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Anthropic has declined to comment on the posts by its employees or the situation with the AISI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: A Cabinet Office spokesperson did not comment on whether the latest model had been withheld from the AISI - instead saying it "continues to collaborate closely with industry partners, including Anthropic, to make models safer".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: In his post, which has been viewed more than 10 million times, Hubinger said "we really do earnestly believe" AI poses a species-ending risk to humans.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: "I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to," he added.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Hubinger works in AI alignment, which aims to build human ethical ideas and principles into the technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: In other words, it aims to keep it on track with what humans value.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Many leading researchers say those attempts appear to be failing, as demonstrated by a string of incidents this summer where AI agents - AI systems that are allowed to operate autonomously - carried out cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: OpenAI , Anthropic and Meta all disclosed hacks carried out by their AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: In Anthropic's safety report from August , external , it wrote there was a low risk of its models becoming misaligned with a hypothetical powerful organisation's desires, causing it to exploit or tamper with its systems.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: It also said there was a similarly low risk of highly capable AI being able to "perform automated research and development" which could cause "catastrophic harm initiated by the AI".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: But it said it was "less confident in this assessment" than it was previously.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: "We are seeing early signs of potential acceleration," it wrote.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Leading figures in the AI field have been raising the alarm about the safety threat the tech poses for years, with the heads of OpenAI, Google Deepmind and Anthropic saying as much in 2023 .
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: But those warnings have become much more stark in recent weeks, as evidence emerges that firms may be struggling to control AI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Earlier this month, OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for "extreme caution" over AI's progress, warning more intervention may be needed to ensure "humans remain in control of the future".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: Major figures in the space have been calling for AI development to be slowed in recent months, including Anthropic bosses Dario Amodei and Jared Kaplan.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'

sentences.text: In an open letter signed by 1,300 staff members of AI firms , external , they called for the US government to "support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development".

sentences.text: Here's what it means for you.

sentences.text: Writing a will is probably not on the to-do lists of most 27-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: But Erin Atkinson has already decided what should happen to her money and belongings when she dies.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "At first it felt quite surreal because you associate wills with older people," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Erin works in psychological research at a London university and moved to the capital from Bristol four years ago.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: She now rents and, although she did not want to share her exact salary, does not see herself as particularly wealthy.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Even so, she has already decided where some of her things should go.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Her £7,000 car will go to her sister.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: A gold necklace given to her by her partner will go back to him.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: And she has asked for some of her money to go to a cause that matters deeply to her.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "One thing that's close to my heart is an endometriosis charity," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "It felt really empowering that I could have that written down to say I want X amount donated." The 2025 National Wills Report found that just one in five 18 to 24-year-olds has a will in place.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: That rises to 33% of 22 to 34-year-olds, compared with 56% of people aged over 55.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Erin has left her £7,000 car to her sister and a gold necklace to her partner Writing a will can seem daunting and expensive.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: But there are ways to get one written for free or at a lower cost.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: For example, every November, Will Aid , external works with solicitors who volunteer their time and waive their fee for writing a basic will.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Members of a trade union may also benefit from a free will writing service, according to Citizens Advice. , external For many young people, making a will may not seem necessary, particularly if they feel they have little to leave behind.

sentences.text: Sophia Maslin, founder of Morby, a website that allows people to create wills online, says the idea that you need to own a lot before making a will is one of the biggest misconceptions she comes across.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "People believe they don't own enough.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: But actually, if you've got some sort of savings, investments, pensions, your social media accounts, if you've got pets, even funeral wishes, these are all things to think about," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: For Erin, the idea of making a will first came up when her friend bought a home.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Then she began seeing Maslin talking about wills on TikTok.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Maslin had shared the story of her cousin, who died young without a will, and how complicated things became for her family.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Sophia Maslin created Morby in 2024, inspired by her own family's experience of dealing with wills Seeing her story made Erin think more seriously about making one for herself, while seeing the effect of her own grandmother's will on her family also influenced her.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "My grandma passed and she had a will and it was very complex because we have quite a large family.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: The process also made Erin see she had more financial assets than she realised, such as premium bonds.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: At the start of summer, in the pillared room in 10 Downing Street, Andy Burnham looked out at his new special advisers, the few dozen political officials tasked with driving hundreds of thousands of civil servants to deliver his government's agenda.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Some had been with him in Manchester or Makerfield.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Others had spent the past few months trying everything to prevent his hostile takeover of Sir Keir Starmer's government - and the new prime minister showed he was aware of it, going out of his way to praise those who had stayed on, for their efforts in the preceding years.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: At that meeting, Burnham's team mapped out four key moments in the coming months.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: First, the return to Parliament in September, when Burnham and other leading ministers would make their first statements to MPs.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Second, Labour's annual conference at the end of September - Burnham's first as leader.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Third, the Budget, taking place on 28 October.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: And fourth, the 10-year plan for Britain which Burnham intends to unveil in November.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: As MPs prepare to leave Parliament on Tuesday for almost a month and party conference season gets underway, the first phase of that route map is almost complete - enough for figures at all levels of the Labour Party to begin answering some questions about the shape of this new government.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Most importantly, perhaps, how new actually is it?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Does Burnham represent continuity or change?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: That question is especially relevant because those Labour MPs who pushed for Sir Keir to be replaced always fell into two broad camps: those who wanted a change of style and emphasis but continuity in policy, and those who wanted a major shift in policy.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Both groups saw what they wanted in Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Andy Burnham speaks during his first Cabinet meeting since becoming prime minister Going by the words of the new prime minister himself, he represents a profound break with the past, and not only the immediate past.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: In his first speech as Labour leader in July, Burnham described his ascendancy as "the most significant change moment in our politics for 40 years".
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: That is the timeframe he has returned to again and again, signalling not just a desire to reverse issues he believes stem from the Thatcher era but also to break with aspects of the Labour governments since then, including his immediate predecessor's.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Some in government are already quietly questioning, though, whether the ambition of that rhetoric can be squared with the early signals emerging from the Treasury under the new Chancellor John Healey.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Who's in Andy Burnham's cabinet?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: In interviews over recent weeks, and especially in his first major speech on Monday , Healey has said he will stick to Rachel Reeves's commitments not to increase the main rates of income tax, national insurance and VAT, as well as her rules on government borrowing.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: In the speech, he promised to "control public spending", and hailed Reeves for beginning to "recover Britain's fiscal discipline".
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: It led to opposition parties labelling Healey a continuity chancellor.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: A similar critique is being voiced among some of his government colleagues.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Most are more generous for now, arguing that Healey's first imperative - especially at a time of turmoil in the global bond markets - is reassurance, and that the Budget is the moment for him to show how he plans to substantiate Burnham's rhetoric.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: And finding ways to boost regional growth has been one of Healey's major causes since he was a junior minister at the Treasury more than 20 years ago - long before it was at the heart of Burnham's political personality.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: There is no question, though, that this week the minister who most starkly signalled change from the previous government was a man who coveted Healey's job - Ed Miliband, who was instead appointed foreign secretary.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: The sanctions announcement was received with near-universal warmth from Labour MPs, itself a marker of change from the Starmer government.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: It was also seen as a sign of the ability of Miliband in particular, but this government in general, to drive its agenda through the civil service machine.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: "There is a much clearer sense now from No 10 of what they want," one official who worked under Sir Keir as well as Burnham says.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: "Before there was a bit too much of 'let us know your ideas for what we should do', now it's 'this is what the PM wants, give us options to deliver it'." sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: According to one present, the prime minister said: "We need to be on the front foot.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Let's get on and do things.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: The new attorney general, Ellie Reeves, has pared back rules introduced under Sir Keir which some ministers believed forced them to be over-cautious about legal risk, thereby slowing down or blocking new policies altogether.

sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: "If we can't microchip cats without getting tied up in red tape, it should come as no surprise the public is losing faith that governments can get things done," she said.

sentences.text: As Burnham moves into the next phase of his autumn, there is a recognition from some around him that he will need to produce some more significant policies to underpin his rhetoric.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Those in government familiar with early work on fleshing out his commitment to "public control" of essential services insist the direction of travel is truly radical.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Haigh is responsible for this, chairing a taskforce on how to reverse "over-privatisation" specifically of housing, water, energy and transport.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: Burnham may offer more details on these policies at Labour's conference, while he is likely to wait until after then to show his hand on whether he wants continuity or change when it comes to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's reforms to the legal immigration system - a much more divisive issue among Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: And whatever their differences on policy, Labour MPs are united on one thing.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: The fundamental reason they installed a new prime minister was because many of them believed that continuing on the same path meant losing the next general election.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out

sentences.text: For them, a long-term improvement in Labour's poll ratings would be the most important change of them all.

sentences.text: Angela Rayner has defended her decision to pause plans to redraw local council boundaries, saying she wanted to ensure they would survive legal challenge.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The local government secretary also told the BBC she wanted to be "clear-eyed" about what the planned shake-up in 16 areas of England was likely to achieve.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It comes after earlier this week she abandoned proposals in four other areas, in the face of legal threats from Reform and Conservative-led authorities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The surprise announcement on Monday has thrown the reorganisation plans into doubt, and drawn criticism from local leaders preparing for the changes.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Councils in affected areas have been drawing up proposals and consulting with residents since the reorganisation was announced in late 2024, in a process that is already thought to have cost millions of pounds.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast, Rayner conceded the decision to press pause had been "difficult" and she understood local authorities had put a "lot of time and effort" into their plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: But she added she wanted to have "all the information" about the proposals before going ahead with them, after her reappointment to her cabinet role under Andy Burnham, ten months after her resignation last year .
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "I got the legal advice and I hadn't had the time to review and to go through all of that, and court cases were looming," she told the podcast.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "If I'm making a decision that is highly likely to be in legal challenge, I want to make sure I've dotted my i's and crossed my t's," she added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Rayner also said she wanted was "really clear-eyed on where we were going" with the plans, after Burnham had asked her to look again at the blueprints, which were announced by her predecessor Steve Reed.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson Plans for major overhaul of councils halted Council to take government to court over reforms In her announcement on Monday, Rayner said she was withdrawing plans to reorganise councils in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Those proposals, announced in March, were already subject to legal challenges from Reform-led councils in Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk, and the Conservative-led administration in Hampshire, which were lodged over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also said she wanted to review plans for 16 other areas, including 14 announced by Reed days before Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister and reappointed her to her old role.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Some councils affected by those plans, including Kent and Leicestershire, had threatened similar bids to challenge the lawfulness of the decision-making process.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The government has argued that the plans, which will abolish remaining two-tier areas in England where county and district councils share responsibility for services, would make local government more effective and cost efficient.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: However, critics said the plans would not save money, while diverting resources from front-line services and leaving councils more remote from their communities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Others have also complained that the reorganisation could stymie or delay parallel efforts to merge councils into regional authorities led by mayors, which Burnham has cited as a key part of his economic plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Elsewhere in her interview, Rayner said Labour under Sir Keir should have been quicker to recognise a Palestinian state, having promised to do so as a "contribution to a renewed peace process" at the last election.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Starmer took the move in September last year, having spent much of the prior year  resisting pressure to do so from Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "It's always been Labour policy to recognise a Palestinian state, and it felt like we got there too late.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It was something that should have been really clear," she said.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also denied that UK sanctions against Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, announced on Tuesday , had been made to help Labour ahead of the forthcoming by-election in Holborn and St Pancras in central London.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Pointing to the fact that Western allies had also announced sanctions, she said: "The French and the Canadians are not going to be like 'oh well, we'll just signal something to help you with a local by-election in London'".
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Reflecting on her return to government, she said a "big difference" between Burnham and his predecessor in Downing Street was his inclination to tell "the story of why we're doing something" in government.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She said both men shared "passion and the commitment" to deliver for Labour in office, but added: "Andy is probably more like me, in terms of [he] wears his heart on his sleeve".
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Colin Sutton was elected as Norfolk's Police and Crime Commissioner two months ago A newly elected £79,000-a-year police commissioner is facing criticism for announcing a 127-date national theatre tour.

sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: After retiring from the Metropolitan Police, Sutton wrote a book about the case, which was later turned into an ITV drama .
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: He has also become a regular commentator in the media and last year was named as Reform's national policing and crime advisor.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: Private vets will be able to diagnose bluetongue after examining affected animals Vets will now be able to diagnose bluetongue virus in livestock so farmers do not have to wait for confirmed test results under changes announced by the government.

sentences.text: The potentially deadly virus, which affects sheep and cattle as well as other animals, continues to spread with confirmed cases on 1,048 farms , external in the UK - more than half are in Devon and Cornwall.

sentences.text: Anthony Lee and his wife Laura pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have pleaded guilty to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.

sentences.text: On Thursday at Southwark Crown Court, Anthony Lee pleaded guilty to two offences and Laura Lee pleaded guilty to one offence.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: They will be sentenced in October.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: The trials of 10 other defendants will take place in September 2027 and January 2028.

sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet
