sentences.text: Friends Amelia (left) and Beatrice (right) are living at home when they start university this September More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In 2017, it was closer to one in five.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Beatrice is going to the University of Manchester to study maths and plans to commute by train, a journey which can take about 50 minutes in total.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "My first choice was Manchester and then my second was Liverpool, so I knew I could commute," she says, adding that the price of accommodation would have been "a few grand a year".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Amelia, who is going to study at Liverpool John Moores University - approximately 20 minutes away by train - says the accommodation she found was between £300 and £400 a week.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Although neither is looking forward to the commute, both are still hoping they can get the full experience of university while living at home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: My three-hour university commute is worth the £7,000 saving on halls However, fellow student Jessica, who is also going to study at Liverpool John Moores University, feels she will miss out.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: She says she would have loved to live on campus and enjoy student life, but the price of renting is "ridiculous" and "insane".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "I have a part-time job as everything is so expensive, and then commuting is going to kill a lot of my free time as well," she says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "It is a bit sad really when you think about it." But she is pleased that staying at home means she will still be able to have her mum and dad's cooked dinners.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Earlier this year, BBC News followed the daily journey of one first-year student who said she was saving over £7,000 on accommodation by commuting 90 minutes into Manchester each day from home.

sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem This July, during Britain's record-breaking hot summer, a curious row broke out on X over climate science.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Reform's deputy leader Richard Tice shared a Telegraph article headlined: "Heatwaves caused by fall in pollution." He said cleaner air, rather than carbon dioxide, was behind higher temperatures and claimed the public had been "gaslit".
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: He was wrong to suggest that carbon dioxide is not the primary driver of global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But the science he was distorting is real - and much more interesting than his original claim.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The fossil fuels that we've been burning for more than a century produce two very different kinds of pollution.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: As is well known, carbon dioxide warms the Earth.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But less well-known is sulphur pollution, which forms vast numbers of tiny particles in the air and reflects sunlight back into space, partly counteracting the warming effect of carbon.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Thanks to clean-air policies around the world - like the US's Acid Rain Program in the early 1990s, that reduced gas pollution from power plants - sulphur emissions are falling sharply while carbon dioxide emissions remain near record highs.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists increasingly believe the loss of that cooling effect is slightly speeding up global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The past three years were the three warmest ever recorded, and the Met Office says 2027 is "very likely" to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And away from social media, the argument over Tice's tweet raised an even more interesting - and worrying - question.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Is it possible that our planet is actually more sensitive to greenhouse gases than we imagined?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And if so, might the climate be changing more rapidly than we feared?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Global temperatures jump around naturally from year to year.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: El Niño, for example, a natural warming of the Pacific Ocean, can temporarily push them higher.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So a run of record hot years does not necessarily mean the underlying rate of global warming has increased.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Reto Knutti and his team at ETH Zurich have tried to strip out the effects of El Niño and other natural fluctuations to reveal the underlying trend.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "It's pretty clear that the rate of warming has accelerated," says Knutti, a professor of climate physics at the Swiss university and a former co-ordinating lead author for the IPCC - the UN-backed body that produces the world's most authoritative assessments of climate science.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: A separate study published this year reached a similar conclusion after accounting for several major natural influences.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And it seems aerosols are playing a role.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Burning coal and oil releases sulphur dioxide, which forms tiny particles known as sulphate aerosols.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: These particles are bright and reflect some sunlight before it can reach and warm the planet's surface.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Pollution from ships can create bright trails through clouds, visible from space You've probably heard the greenhouse analogy used to explain global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Gases like carbon dioxide make it harder for heat to escape from the Earth, rather like the glass windows of a greenhouse.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Well, sulphur pollution acts a bit like dust on the greenhouse windows.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The more dust that gathers on those windows, the less sunlight gets inside, and the slower the greenhouse heats up in the first place.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Dr Øivind Hodnebrog, a principal researcher at Cicero, the Norwegian climate research institute, has studied how falling aerosol pollution affects the climate.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "Sulphate aerosols, they are really small particles, but they are bright particles," he says.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: As well as reflecting sunlight, aerosols also cool the planet by changing the formation of clouds.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Aerosols act like tiny seeds around which water vapour can condense, making some clouds brighter or longer-lived.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Pollution from ships can even create bright trails through marine clouds visible from space.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So more aerosols mean brighter clouds and more reflection, and so less warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Emissions have fallen sharply in Europe, North America and China, while new rules have also reduced sulphur pollution from shipping.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: In our greenhouse analogy, it's as if we've wiped some of the dust away from the windows of the greenhouse, allowing in more sunlight.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And while carbon dioxide remains in the climate system for centuries, sulphate aerosols survive in the atmosphere for just days or weeks.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So when sulphur emissions fall, their cooling effect disappears almost immediately.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The effect is strongest where sulphur pollution has fallen fastest.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: One study estimates it has added around half a degree to summer warming in western-central Europe since 1980.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Prof Piers Forster, a climate scientist at the University of Leeds and another senior author of the IPCC's most recent assessment, estimates that declining aerosol pollution may now be adding around 0.05C to 0.1C of warming per decade.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But aerosols can only explain part of the recent acceleration in warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Greenhouse gases remain much more important.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Forster estimates they are currently adding around 0.2C of warming globally per decade.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "It is a very significant contribution," he says of the aerosol effect, "but it is not as important as the greenhouse gas contribution by quite a long way." "The aerosols have masked some of the greenhouse gas warming from earlier," is how Hodnebrog explains it.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "Masked" - that's an interesting word he uses.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: What he means is cleaner air is not causing the underlying warming; it is removing some of the cooling that had been holding that warming back.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So if cleaner air is only responsible for part of the recent acceleration in global warming, what else is at work?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: To see what else might be going on, scientists zoom out and look at the Earth as a whole: how much energy it absorbs from the Sun, and how much heat it loses back into space.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists call the difference Earth's energy imbalance.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Cleaner air is part of that picture.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Fewer sulphate particles mean less sunlight is reflected away - in our greenhouse analogy, the windows are cleaner.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: For a long time, the Earth has been absorbing more energy than it loses.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That surplus is what warms the planet.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But there's still lots of uncertainty.

sentences.text: Dorothea Bate, born in 1878, had little formal education but a fascination with wildlife and nature A pioneering fossil hunter who was one of the first women to be employed by the Natural History Museum has been recognised with a national blue plaque.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Dorothea Bate, who died in 1951 aged 72, "transformed our understanding of prehistoric animals and ancient environments" through her research, Historic England said.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She has been recognised with a plaque at the Natural History Museum , in Tring, Hertfordshire, which notes in its inscription that the palaeontologist was the "Officer-in-Charge of this museum from 1948".
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Bate was born in Carmarthen, Wales, in 1878 and developed a fascination with the natural world from an early age.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She moved with her family to rural Gloucestershire as a young woman and spent hours exploring the surrounding countryside and caves, collecting fossils.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She had little formal education, instead largely teaching herself, and in 1900 asked for work behind the scenes at the Natural History Museum in London.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Her determination impressed museum staff, earning her a position as an assistant and beginning an association with the institution that would last more than 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She published her first scientific paper, A Short Account Of A Bone Cave In The Carboniferous Limestone Of The Wye Valley, in 1901.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Bate went on to undertake expeditions across the Mediterranean, often travelling alone to remote caves in search of evidence of ancient life.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: In Cyprus, she discovered a previously unknown species of dwarf elephant and in 1909, while in the Balearics, she discovered the myotragus - an extinct goat-like antelope.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She achieved more than 80 published scientific papers, despite spending most of her career without a permanent paid position.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: In 2017, a blue plaque was dedicated to Bate at Napier House in Carmarthen where she was born.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: "She used this drive to make sense of ancient life through fragments of bone, bringing it to life once again," they said.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: "Her research transformed our understanding of prehistoric animals and ancient environments.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: "Not only does her work continue to be invaluable in the field that she helped to establish, but as one of the first women to be employed by the Natural History Museum she was instrumental in paving the way for future women in science.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: "This plaque ensures that her pioneering contributions to science receives the wider recognition it deserves." Heritage minister Baroness Twycross said Bate's achievements "helped break through the glass ceiling and paved the way for women in palaeontology".
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Dr Sandra Knapp, director of research at the Natural History Museum, said: "The role of women scientists in natural history is often hidden - but Dorothea Bate's work with fossil mammals was both innovative and set a path for others, despite obstacles.

sentences.text: Sarah Hickey is part of a team which keeps nearly 20,000 acres of upland healthy High up on a Manx hillside, Sarah Hickey effortlessly pushes a metre-long metal rod into the wet ground until it disappears almost to her hands.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: "This is pretty deep here," she says, reading the markings on the probe.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Beneath her boots is peat, built up over thousands of years and consisting of partially decayed plants and organic matter.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Hickey is the island's Peatland Officer and part of an Uplands team of just three, who, between them, manage about 8,000 hectares of the Island's hills.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Hickey's job is to find the parts of that landscape which have been damaged, and inject life into it.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Peat is partially decomposed vegetation that builds up in waterlogged ground over centuries, storing more carbon than any other soil on Earth.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: "It's important to keep that carbon locked away and not released to the atmosphere," Hickey says.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Much of that carbon has stayed locked away, but not all of it.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: The island's uplands were largely stripped of trees by the 17th century, and with little timber left to burn, islanders turned to the hills for fuel instead.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Peat would be cut into blocks and left to dry; peat made a good, slow-burning fuel, and for generations it was what Manx households cooked on and heated their homes with.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: The practice was banned in 2020, but the bare faces that cutting left behind are still collapsing and eroding today, washing sediment down into reservoirs.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: One of the sites that has been repaired, which now hosts a plethora of wildlife Repairs start with a digger light enough not to cause fresh damage, which pulls the bare peat back to a gentler slope and folds the vegetation over it.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: What is left exposed is protected with bio logs, then held down under netting, which keeps the ground shaded and damp so new vegetation can take hold.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: The real engineer of a healthy bog, experts say though, is sphagnum moss.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: "It grows in peatland habitats, but it also creates them," Hickey says.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: It holds huge amounts of water, slowing rain as it moves downhill, reducing flooding and filtering out sediment before it reaches the reservoir.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: It is also, she says, more fire-resistant; peat in good condition can be up to 90% water, which is increasingly important as wildfires become more common during summer months.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Peatland stores more carbon than any other land-based habitat on Earth, Hickey says It matters for wildlife too.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: Ground-nesting birds such as hen harriers rely on open, treeless bog, safe from predators that would otherwise perch and watch for prey, while the wet ground breeds the invertebrates chicks are fed on.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: The reward can arrive fast.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: After installing coir logs on one site last year, Hickey and colleagues sat down for tea beside the new pools they had created.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: "Straight away there were dragonflies in that pool laying eggs," she says.
sentences.article_title: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs

sentences.text: "It was amazing to see what a difference these little features are making." sentences.text: Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons.

sentences.text: The findings, made in the firm's recent threat intelligence report, is the latest in a growing series of warnings from AI researchers and industry insiders about the technology's potential risks to humanity .

sentences.text: The warnings have prompted calls to action, with US Senator Bernie Sanders demanding a pause on advanced AI development and a ban on artificial superintelligence.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The company published its latest threat intelligence report , external on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Such reports have become a regular feature across the AI industry as firms seek to demonstrate how they identify and disrupt attempts to misuse their models.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: This includes Google, which wrote on Tuesday , external that a person had attempted to use its AI tool, Gemini, to obtain a "complete, step-by-step technical guide for synthesizing weaponised biological agents".

sentences.text: Claude, Anthropic's AI model was also used by actors linked to a Russia-based cyber espionage campaign and by an Iranian propaganda institution, according to its report.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The cases of concern detected over the past eight months ranged from fake dating apps and hotel Wifi scams, to surveillance built to identify dissidents.

sentences.text: Anthropic has also accused Chinese AI firms of trying to replicate Claude's capabilities.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The lengthy report lists cases in which suspected state-sponsored groups, criminals, spyware vendors, state propaganda institutions and politically motivated individuals misused its technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "Malicious use" of its Claude Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus models was disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026, it said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: None of the misuse cases involved Claude Fable or the powerful Mythos-class models, with the exception of one instance of distillation - the process for training smaller AI models using larger, more expensive models.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: As well as detecting the use of its models for cyber and influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud and weapon development, Anthropic said it had blocked scientists who used its AI in ways that could support biological weapons development.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The report highlighted "five case studies of actors using our models in ways that could support biological weapons development".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Biological misuse, it said, is "one of the most serious risks of frontier AI model".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Without the correct safeguards, such capabilities "could have catastrophic consequences", Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "The same information that can be used to develop a biological weapon could also be used to develop, for example, a vaccine or a cure for a disease," Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, told the New York Times , external it was "an incredibly nuanced situation".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Scientists may have found evidence of dark matter for the first time in an underground lab Scientists believe they may be one step closer to detecting dark matter for the first time, but the findings have not been verified by independent researchers.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Scientists from the University of Bristol were part of a two-year study to try and measure the invisible substance thought to make up over 85% of the universe.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Using a sensitive detector in an an underground laboratory in the US, the researchers saw an atom and mystery particle colliding.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Lead researcher physicist Dr Sam Eriksen said it could be "the first step in understanding dark matter as a particle", but further research could also reveal that the particle is not related to dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "Following a huge amount of scientific effort, this is incredibly exciting," the University of Bristol senior research associate added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Although scientists have long been certain of the existence of dark matter, because it is invisible as it reflects no light.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: While it is thought to make up the majority of mass in the universe, it has never been directly detected.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: It is managed by the US Department of Energy's Sanford Underground Research Facility in South Dakota - the deepest laboratory in the US at nearly a mile beneath the ground.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Scientists studied data from one of the world's most sensitive dark matter detectors To search for dark matter, LZ uses extremely sensitive light detectors to capture particle interactions.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: The study found one particle interaction which could potentially have been caused by a Weakly Interacting Massive Particle, (WIMP), which scientists believe make up dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: But there is currently low statistical evidence in it being a true breakthrough. 'I would be dead if I had not learnt about little-known law' How many times has Clare's Law been used in the West of England?
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Crews still battling industrial fire after blasts heard The findings were revealed at a conference in Japan on Tuesday, but the research has yet to undergo peer-review by other scientists.

sentences.text: The findings have been rated 2.6 sigma, which is the system that marks the statistical significance of discoveries.

sentences.text: The normal threshold is five.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "With only one event, we don't want to get ahead of ourselves," said Professor Rick Gaitskell from Brown University.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "We are not claiming to have seen dark matter.

sentences.text: "To date none provide a convincing explanation," he said.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Declan Craggs is urging everyone in the town to help tackle the mess caused by pigeons Pigeons have been leaving a town's High Street looking dirty and efforts to deter the birds from congregating have failed, a mayor has said.

sentences.text: Declan Craggs, the mayor of Diss, Norfolk, said Diss Town Council has tried using ultrasonic sound devices and employing a falconer's hawks to scare the pigeons away from Mere Street, but nothing has worked.

sentences.text: While many locals agree with the council's actions, others feel the pigeons were being unfairly demonised.
sentences.article_title: Town gets in a flap over High Street pigeon mess

sentences.text: Earlier this year, Norwich City Council has also similarly struggled to find a solution for a large population of pigeons at the market .
sentences.article_title: Town gets in a flap over High Street pigeon mess

sentences.text: Craggs said: "It is about taking ownership of the town you live in and the business you run.
sentences.article_title: Town gets in a flap over High Street pigeon mess

sentences.text: "If everyone did their little bit, I think it would dramatically increase the appearance of Mere Street." The council has asked businesses in the town's centre to consider putting spikes and other deterrents on their building's front ledges.

sentences.text: Pigeon droppings and feathers are making Mere Street look dirty, residents have said Craggs has urged people to stop feeding the pigeons, with signs put up across the town - yet, he said, it has not stopped the problem.

sentences.text: "Some people are of the opinion pigeons have as much of a right to be here as we do, which is why we haven't taken these steps [to cull them] and are looking at just trying to keep the area tidy on a day-to-day basis," Craggs said.

sentences.text: A Naga delegation visited the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford last year More than three dozen sets of human remains taken during the British colonial rule of India and Myanmar are set to be returned to their ancestral home by a museum.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: Skulls and bones belonging to the Naga people of northeastern India and Myanmar - formerly known as Burma - have been displayed at the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford for more than a century.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: In 2020, the museum removed all human remains from public display as part of what the it called a "decolonisation process" - including the ancestral Naga remains.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: The museum has now announced that a formal decision has been made by the University of Oxford Council to return the 39 ancestral human remains to their homeland.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: "They've been here in a foreign land for more than a century," Dr Vihuto Asumi, President of the Sumî Hoho Naga tribe, said of the remains.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: Many were acquired by John Henry Hutton, a colonial administrator in the Indian Civil Service and an anthropologist, who handed them to the museum more than a century ago.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: Among the museum's Naga collection - which contains several thousand items - are 219 items listed as human remains, 39 ancestral human remains and 178 objects that are thought to contain human hair.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: The latest announcement concerns only the ancestral remains, and follows a declaration made by a Naga delegation visiting Oxford in 2025, in which the group requested the objects be returned.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: The Naga will then accompany the remains of their ancestors home, with some returning for the first time in more than a century.
sentences.article_title: Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Manasse Lomachar would like the discovery of gold to improve life in his village A goat herder from a remote area of western Kenya has told the BBC his discovery of a golden nugget has sparked a gold rush, overwhelming his small village over the last few weeks.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: When people found out that 33-year-old Manasse Lomachar had sold his three grams of gold for 36,000 Kenyan shillings ($280; £205) several weeks ago, he believes this led to the arrival of thousands of prospectors in Cheporor.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: And it is true that what last month was just bushland and rough grazing ground near the village is now scarred by pits, mounds of earth and makeshift mining camps.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: It is not clear if was Lomachar's lucky find or other recent discoveries that sparked the excitement.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: But local authorities estimate that about 10,000 people arrived at the height of the rush.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Even a small amount of the precious metal can transform the futures of these men and women - from Kenya and neighbouring Uganda - many of whose precarious lives rest on an unreliable farming income.
sentences.article_title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?

sentences.text: Large numbers of people have been searching through the earth and rocks for any sign of the precious metal People do sometimes pan for gold in these parts - but rarely find anything significant.

sentences.text: Chinese President Xi Jinping and India Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Brics summit in Russia in 2024 The US is not a member of Brics, yet President Donald Trump's shadow will loom large over the group's summit in Delhi this weekend.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Leaders from 11 Brics nations - including host India, China, Russia, Brazil, South Africa, the UAE and Iran, with Saudi Arabia attending as an invited member - will hold talks on a wide range of issues.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: But few will be as consequential as the impact of President Trump's policies.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The war in Iran and the ever-present threat of White House tariffs, directed at both US adversaries and allies, have destabilised global energy markets and has often left the global economy guessing the future.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: It is against this backdrop that Brics leaders are meeting.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Yet the group is unlikely to produce a consensus statement that openly calls out the US or lays out a coordinated strategy to counter President Trump's policies and geopolitics.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: That is partly because Brics itself is deeply divided over how far it should go in challenging Washington.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: "India cannot afford to have a joint statement that rails against Washington," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: He expects any criticism of US policies to be "vague and indirect", reflecting the sharply divergent interests within the expanded group.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: While Russia and Iran may push for the group to take a clearer stand against President Trump, the geopolitical realities within Brics are likely to make that difficult.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: India, which is reportedly in the final stages of a trade deal with the US, will not want a statement that could upset the White House.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: China, too, may be wary of being seen as using Brics to target Washington.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Then there is the UAE, which has come under Iranian attack during Tehran's retaliation against US and Israeli strikes.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The Gulf state, which hosts US military bases, is unlikely to support a statement that helps Tehran's cause.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Kugelman says Brics has become more significant through its expansion, but that has also made consensus harder.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump with India's Modi during a bilateral meeting at the G7 summit in France in 2026 "You've added a number of members that don't get along," he said, describing the challenge for India as bringing together countries with "a wide array of views and positions on the global order".
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Trump has also been quite vocal against Brics, particularly its efforts to reduce global trade's dependence on the US dollar, commonly known as de-dollarisation.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: He has often warned the group against trying to come up with an alternative currency or take measures to weaken the dollar's dominance in global trade.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: In one such threat, Trump said in November 2024 that Brics countries would face "100% tariffs" if they backed another currency to replace the "mighty US dollar".
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, what can the group realistically deliver?
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Brics' geopolitical and economic heft has grown substantially over the past decade.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: While it will be reluctant to take an openly anti-US or anti-Western position, the group will be looking to build on its existing achievements and demonstrate that it can emerge as an alternative blocs like the G20 and G7.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Brics now accounts for 49% of the world's population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of international trade, according to BBC Monitoring's analysis.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Its most tangible achievement remains the New Development Bank - which has approved billions of dollars in infrastructure and development projects - many of them in countries of the global south.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The group has also created a $100bn contingency reserve arrangement to help members facing financial crises, although it has yet to be tested.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The leaders are also likely to explore ways to make cross-border payments in local currencies easier.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: That will be of particular interest to Moscow and Tehran, both of which face severe US sanctions.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Brics is also expected to continue positioning itself as a voice for the developing nations, collectively pushing for reforms to institutions such as the United Nations, International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, which many developing nations feel do not accurately reflect the new global order.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: For India, in particular, the summit offers an opportunity to strengthen its claim to leadership of the global south.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Many of Delhi's own foreign policy priorities, including multilateralism, a more multipolar world, greater representation for developing countries and freer global trade, align closely with Brics' wider agenda.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: But India will also have to find ways to work around China's considerable influence within Brics and its stronger presence across much of the developing world.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The Modi government has placed a strong emphasis on becoming a "leader or a voice of the Global South", Kugelman says.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: But India's efforts have had "limited success" in making deeper inroads in Africa and Latin America, where China has been more successful.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: With most Brics members coming from developing economies, Kugelman says the expanded grouping gives India an opportunity to deepen ties with countries such as Ethiopia, Brazil and Indonesia and build a stronger profile across Africa and Latin America.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The war in Iran and its economic fallout are expected to be high on the agenda For Delhi, the test will be whether it can secure a consensus statement - often seen as a measure of a host nation's diplomatic success.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: That will be difficult given sharp differences over the Iran war, relations with the US and the future of global trade.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The scale of the challenge was evident in May, when Brics foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement after their summit because of differences over the Iran war, leaving host India to issue a chair's summary instead.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: India will take confidence from its experience as G20 host in 2023, when it managed to secure a joint declaration despite deep divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: But Delhi will also want substantive announcements and to highlight what Brics has already achieved.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: On this, members are likely to agree: none will want the grouping dismissed as merely a "talk shop".
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Leaders are expected to explore ways to strengthen financial cooperation and may make substantive announcements.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: They are also likely to address major geopolitical developments, with any language on the US is expected to be carefully crafted to avoid confrontation.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Washington, for its part, will be watching closely.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Delhi has been converted into a fortress with thousands of security personnel deployed as leaders start arriving for the weekend summit The summit will also provide the setting for several important bilateral meetings.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Chinese President Xi Jinping's meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday will be keenly watched.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: The two countries have been slowly rebuilding ties, although progress has been more cautious than either side might have hoped.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Modi is also due to meet President Vladimir Putin, with the war in Ukraine likely to feature prominently in their discussions.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Modi made a highly public appeal for peace when he met Putin last month on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: While some interpreted his remarks as a rebuke to Moscow, Russia did not see them that way and publicly welcomed Modi's efforts.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Beyond geopolitics, India's growing trade deficit with both Russia and China is also likely to feature in the bilateral discussions.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: But in the end, the group's focus will be on concluding a successful summit as it would add further weight to Brics' influence.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: And for host India, it would also be a diplomatic and geopolitical achievement at a time when Delhi is seeking to reassert its international influence.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Kugelman says the stakes are particularly high for India at this summit.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Delhi, he argues, has been somewhat overshadowed by Pakistan's recent diplomatic role in the Middle East, including its involvement in mediation efforts around the Iran war.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: "This is an important opportunity for India to reassert its global significance and its global leadership," he says.
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: "That is one reason why the stakes are high." The summit, he adds, is in some ways "more important for India as host than it is for the Brics grouping as a whole".
sentences.article_title: Trump shadow looms large over Brics as Modi hosts Putin and Xi in Delhi

sentences.text: Jaws of early human settlers showed unusual dental wear which researchers linked to sucking whole betel nuts Humans may have been using mind-altering substances far earlier than scientists had once thought, new research indicates.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: The evidence shows that betel nuts were used as drugs by some Indonesian communities up to 25,000 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: Scientists from Griffith University in Australia found unusual patterns in the skeletal remains of early human foragers, which they linked to the sucking of betel nuts.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: Professor Adam Brumm, who led the research, said this may be the "earliest evidence for drug use anywhere in the world".
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: When consumed, betel nuts induce a sense of mild euphoria and heightened awareness In the new study, published in Science Advances, the researchers reported the discovery of rare skeletal remains of two early human foragers from the Indonesian island of Sulawesi.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: One dated to 25,000-16,000 years ago and the other to 7,600-6,300 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: Both of the hunter-gatherers showed an unusual dental wear pattern with deep, rounded tooth grooves, which the researchers found was caused by sucking whole betel nuts.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: When consumed, betel nuts – seeds of the betel or Areca catechu palm – induce a sense of mild euphoria and heightened awareness.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: Brumm said: "Although poorly known in western societies, it is the world's fourth most widely used psychoactive substance, after alcohol, caffeine and nicotine." It had previously been thought that drug-taking began after the advent of farming, beginning with fermented alcohol drinks about 13,000 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: However, that theory "fails to account for the possibility that very ancient drug-taking lies at the roots of our most commonly used psychoactive substances", according to Brumm.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: The mixture is popular in South and South East Asia, and is chewed by about one-tenth of the globe's population.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: Researchers conducted experiments where they soaked betel nuts in artificial saliva, and found that just sucking on intact betel nuts released enough of the psychoactive compounds to alter brain function.
sentences.article_title: Drug use may have begun 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, research finds

sentences.text: The effects of sucking betel nuts may have been milder than modern quid chewing, but the team suggested that the habit was significant enough to cause severe gum disease.

sentences.text: Letsile Tebogo helped Botswana to 4x400m gold at the World Relays on home soil in Gaborone in May Olympic 200m champion Letsile Tebogo will return to Budapest for the Ultimate Championships next week, but the Hungarian capital is more than just another stop on the athletics calendar for the Botswana sprinter.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: It is the city where the 23-year-old announced himself to the world and where his mother Seratiwa watched him make history for his country by claiming two medals at the 2023 World Championships.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: This time Seratiwa will not be cheering on her son from the stands, having passed away in May 2024 after a short illness.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Having shared a close relationship with his mother - one she described as being more like a "brother and sister bond" - Tebogo admits that returning without her is difficult.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I haven't really looked into the fact that I'm going now to Budapest without my mom," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "It's just been a bumpy ride having to think about it and having to continue with the grind." Three years ago, Seratiwa surprised her son by travelling to Budapest to watch the then 20-year-old compete in his first senior global championships.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Tebogo won silver in the 100m and bronze in the 200m - the first World Championship medals claimed by a male athlete from Botswana.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: He also became the first African man to win a World Championship medal in the 100m.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Seratiwa told BBC Sport Africa at the time that she was "proud" of what her son had achieved.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: For all the memories the city holds, Tebogo says there is also a source of strength in returning to the place where his mother witnessed one of the defining moments of his career.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I believe she's always there with me in spirit and in days where giving up is an option," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: A year on from his success at the 2023 World Championships, Tebogo scaled greater heights by becoming Botswana's first Olympic champion when he won the 200m at the Paris 2024 Games, carrying his mother's initials on both his shoes and fingernails as a tribute.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: He returns to Budapest as one of the faces of a new competition created to bring together the sport's best performers.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: The Ultimate Championships is a biennial global event designed to crown the best of the best in a track and field season.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: The three-day end-of-season competition includes Olympic champions, world champions, Diamond League winners and the year's other leading performers.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: The inaugural edition in Budapest, which runs from 11-13 September, has a $10m (£7.41m) prize pot - the highest in track and field history according to organisers World Athletics - with each gold medallist taking home $150,000 (£111,000).
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Tebogo, who helped Botswana to gold in the 4x400m at the World Relays on home soil earlier this year before registering 200m wins at the Diamond League events in Oslo and Lausanne, says the 200m in Budapest will not only be about looking back.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: He is one of the team captains for the Kids' Athletics Ultimate Challenge, where young people from across the city will be invited to participate in activities at the Gyula Zsivotzky National Athletics Centre the day before the Ultimate Championships begin.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: That will give him the chance to share some of the lessons he has learned since first stepping onto the global stage.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I believe firstly you should start with accountability," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "Think about your preparation, how you want your journey or your season to be, and then also think of unwavering sportsmanship.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Galagodaatte Gnanasara was a trusted ally of former president Gotabaya Rajapaksa Sri Lanka's Supreme Court has overturned a presidential pardon granted to a hardline Buddhist monk and ordered him to serve the remainder of a six-year prison sentence for intimidating the wife of a missing political cartoonist.
